claim: People prefer inferences tied to a shared causal system over equally relevant isolated facts when an analogy is in play (systematicity as a selection constraint). Seen in ratings, forced choice and free prediction.
agent_test: Give the agent a base passage and a target; offer inference candidates (one inside the shared relational system, one outside). Measure how often it picks the system-linked one with and without an explicit map-relations-first step at equal tokens.
note: Re-read 2026-10-31: Exp1 N=48 F(1,44)=18.43; Exp2 N=32 (16/16) .53 vs .12, F(1,28)=20.05; Exp3 N=48 (24/24) F(1,44)=5.15, Passage 2 failed. Earlier N=46 for Exp3 was wrong. No independent-lab replication found.

claim: Systematicity effects on mapping are conditional: in children (5-10) they show mainly when objects are cross-mapped; with consistent object matches mapping is uniformly good. Mapping quality improves with age.
agent_test: Build cross-mapped vs object-consistent story pairs; test whether a typed relation-first mapping step lifts accuracy mainly in the cross-mapped case.

claim: Surface similarity drives retrieval of analogs, while shared causal structure drives judged soundness. Retrieval and evaluation diverge.
agent_test: Retrieve past cases by embedding vs by relational signature; compare hit rate of structurally right cases at equal token budget (figures are in subfield 03).

claim: SME scores a mapping by summing local evidence propagated down to children (weight 0.8), so deeper connected systems score higher. It needs only the form of the representation, not domain knowledge.
agent_test: Implement a code scorer for typed mappings with the same nesting-weighted sum; check agreement with the human-judged best mapping on 30 hand-built pairs.

claim: Greedy merge of kernels gives near-optimal SME mappings in polynomial time (52 of 56 identical to exhaustive), and an SME-based model solved 39 of 45 visual oddity problems; failures were the items hardest for people.
agent_test: Use a greedy scorer in the loop; compare to exhaustive on small pairs for the same disagreement rate.
note: 52/56 (93%) and 39/45 re-opened and confirmed in Forbus et al. 2017.

claim: Rival models (ACME constraint satisfaction, LISA binding capacity) also reproduce the systematicity effects; ACME failed to settle on the unsystematic cross-mapped case without parameter changes. The data do not single out SME.
agent_test: None needed; treat structure mapping as a scoring heuristic, not a unique mechanism.

claim: Comparing two cases (analogical encoding) improves later transfer over studying them separately: meta-analytic d about 0.50-0.60 over 57 experiments; negotiation transfer 50% vs 19%, and 48% vs 16% of dyads.
agent_test: Show the agent two worked cases and require an explicit alignment before solving a third; compare to the two cases shown separately at equal tokens.
note: Alfieri re-read: d=.60 (57 experiments, CI .47-.72) at experiment level, .50 at test level; far transfer .34.

claim: Alignable differences are listed more readily than non-alignable ones, and more so for similar pairs; comparison makes alignment-linked differences salient.
agent_test: In compare steps, require alignable differences first; check whether defect detection rises.

claim: GPT-3-level models matched or beat average humans on zero-shot analogy tasks in the original study, but the advantage mostly disappears on counterfactual variants (permuted alphabets). Replication: humans 0.753, GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452; humans flat across variants.
agent_test: Test the agent on permuted-symbol relation tasks with and without a typed mapping step.
note: Table 2 row labels now read from raw text (humans .753, GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452), no longer inferred. Stevenson 2025 shows the same far-transfer drop for Claude-3.5, GPT-4o, Llama-405B.

claim: With code execution GPT-4 shows no gap to humans on counterfactual letter strings (P=0.496), so part of the failure is procedural, not missing analogy ability. 46% of GPT-4 errors follow a valid alternative rule.
agent_test: Compare free-text mapping vs code-scored mapping on permuted tasks at equal tokens.
note: Webb 2024 re-read (humans N=99/97, P=0.496). Only a code-for-counting test; no direct code-scored vs free-text mapping at equal tokens. PRISM (82.5% code-scored vs 88.5% zero-shot) is the nearest direct comparison and the code score lost.

claim: On story analogies GPT-3 is above chance for near analogies (p=.0039) but not far (p=.065); humans beat GPT-3 (OR=0.37). On story and science analogy benchmarks models trail humans widely (ChatGPT 29-36% vs humans 85.7% on 4-way story identification).
agent_test: Run far-analogy story identification with and without explicit relation extraction plus typed scoring.

claim: Structure mapping over LLM-derived abstractions beats LLM-only on far analogies (Qwen 0.46 vs 0.41; Llama 0.45 vs 0.28), but without abstraction it is at or below chance, and CoT wins on near analogies (0.79 vs 0.69).
agent_test: Hybrid: LLM extracts relational abstractions, code maps; compare to CoT on far vs near items.
note: YARN re-read: MCQ Qwen 0.17 to 0.46, Llama 0.16 to 0.45; mapping with event phrases only is below chance. No parse-accuracy figure exists.

claim: Self-generated analogical exemplars give small gains at best (GSM8K 75.8 vs 75.0; Codeforces 13-15% vs 8-11%), and relevance is not the active ingredient: relevant exemplars (71.5) scored below none (75.5) and random ones (76.3) on GSM8K for GPT-3.5.
agent_test: Do not add a recall-a-similar-problem step without an equal-token ablation against random exemplars.
note: Chen non-math tables: relevant below none on CSQA 70.8 vs 73.4, MBPP 58.2 vs 59.8, GPQA 31.6 vs 34.4 (GPT-3.5); no frontier model tested.

claim: Explicit decomposition before mapping helps on structured analogy tasks (GPT-3 Center 77.2 to 80.0; 2x2Grid 87.8; 3x3Grid 93.2).
agent_test: Decompose into components before mapping vs map directly, at equal tokens.

claim: Fast variants of SME exist: SMTB runs 5-15x faster (corrected from 515x) with about 50% better mappings on large nested domains; neural AMN reaches 95-104% of SME structural score. SME is fragile when one higher-order kernel fails (other correspondences are dropped), but no measured noise-robustness curve exists.
agent_test: If a scorer is built, add a flat first-order fallback so one failed kernel does not zero the rest.
note: 515x was an extraction error for 5-15x. Corpus time SME 70.95 s vs greedy SMTB 5.97 s.

claim: Strong LLMs lack robustness to permuted relational structure: humans are unaffected by permuted pairs while Claude 3, GPT-4 and Llama-405B drop significantly (z -4.0 to -5.5). Human cells were small (15-18).
agent_test: Run the same permuted-pair condition on our agent.
note: Newer models (Claude-3.5, GPT-4o, Llama-405B, GPT 5.2, Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-OSS 120B) still show permuted/far-transfer weakness in d11 and d12, but exact 2025-2026 reasoning-model scores on the Lewis and Mitchell design are not published as numbers.

claim: LLMs solve children's verbal analogies at roughly the 7 to 11 year level (14,006 children, 622 Dutch items), depending on model.
agent_test: None; background.

claim: Relation changes harm analogy acceptance far more than object changes: verb synonym .96, near .60, far .14 vs noun .98/.97/.86. Relation meaning is the key to the match.
agent_test: In the mapping scorer, charge relation mismatch more than object mismatch.

claim: No independent-lab replication of the Clement and Gentner (1991) systematicity-selection effect was found. All three experiments (N=48, 32, 48) come from one lab, and one of three passages failed in Exp 3. Treat it as a single-lab effect with a consistent direction.
agent_test: Run our own selection test: give the agent two true candidate matches, one inside a shared causal system, and check which it keeps.

claim: The one direct code-scored vs free-choice comparison found (PRISM, AnaloBench 4-way, N=200) had the code score at 82.5% against 88.5% for zero-shot GPT-4.1 mini, with different errors (6 vs 18 solo wins, McNemar p=.0227). Dropping the role-abstraction step took the score to 24%, chance. So a code-scored mapping is a complement, and only as good as its extracted roles.
agent_test: Run free-text mapping vs code-scored mapping vs both at equal tokens on a permuted-relation set; report solo wins for each.

claim: 2025-2026 frontier models are still clearly below humans on far analogical mapping. ARCANA pass@3 union: GPT 5.2 48-51%, Gemini 3 Pro 29-43%, Grok 4.1 Fast 19-25%, Claude Opus 4.5 7-9%, against humans 58-69% pass@1. Code-checked concept loops (ConceptSIR) solved 9 of 17 hard tasks. No published number gives a 2025-2026 reasoning model on the Lewis and Mitchell counterfactual letter-string design.
agent_test: Run our agent on counterfactual letter strings and permuted pairs; compare to a plain run with reasoning on.

claim: The representation step is the weak link in LLM plus structure-mapping pipelines: mapping on raw event phrases is below chance (Qwen 0.17 vs 0.25 random on MCQ), abstraction lifts it to 0.46, and removing semantic roles in PRISM drops it to chance. Direct accuracy of LLM-extracted structure against human-built structure has not been published.
agent_test: Hand-build relation graphs for 30 cases; score the agent's extracted graph by edge precision and recall.

claim: For weaker models relevant recalled analogs do not beat none or random off BBH (CSQA 70.8 vs 73.4; MBPP 58.2 vs 59.8; GPQA 31.6 vs 34.4 with GPT-3.5). LLM retrieval of analogous stories from a 200-story bank is near random for long stories (AnaloBench). No study compares structure-first with embedding retrieval at equal tokens, and none tests strong reasoning models on relevance.
agent_test: Retrieve past cases by embedding vs relational signature at equal token budget; measure solved-rate on held-out tasks.

claim: Gentner and Gentner (1983) flowing-waters data are weaker than the textbook story: Exp 1 kept 15 of 36 subjects (F(1,13)=4.53, p<.05); Exp 2 (N=18) supported one prediction and failed the battery prediction. Gentner (1983) itself could not be read, so its core experiments stay unverified.
agent_test: None; background. Do not cite numbers from Gentner 1983.
